== Overview ==

The '''Manifest Scanner''', historically called the '''Cargo Scanner''', is a Class 0 utility module used to inspect a targeted ship's manifest. A completed scan identifies commodities in its cargo hold and occupants recorded in its passenger cabins.<ref name="edwiki-manifest">Elite Dangerous Wiki, [https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Manifest_Scanner Manifest Scanner], accessed 2026-09-16.</ref>

The module provides information only. It does not transfer cargo, open the target's hatch, establish that an attack is legal, or change the legal status of anything it discovers. A [[Hatch Breaker Limpet Controller]] is the separate module used to force cargo from another ship.

A manifest scan is not covert: the target is notified as soon as the scan begins.<ref name="edwiki-manifest" />

== Operation ==

# Install the scanner in a utility mount and assign it to a fire group.
# Deploy hardpoints and select the ship to inspect.
# Move within the fitted scanner's range and keep the target in front of the ship.
# Hold the assigned trigger until the scan completes.
# Review the revealed cargo and passenger information in the target display.

Stock scanners take 10 seconds to complete a scan. Moving outside range or losing the required angle interrupts the process; an incomplete manifest scan must be started again.<ref name="edwiki-manifest" />

The module is commonly used to:

* identify valuable cargo before attempting ship-to-ship piracy;
* confirm whether a ship carries commodities relevant to a mission or encounter;
* inspect a passenger carrier for a named or mission-relevant occupant; and
* detect cargo or passengers that may be stolen or illegal in the current jurisdiction.

Discovering contraband does not give an independent commander the authority of a system-security vessel. Local crime rules still determine whether interdiction, hatch breaking, or weapons fire will produce fines or bounties.

== Standard variants ==

Every stock variant occupies one utility mount, has Class 0 size, weighs 1.3 tonnes, uses a 15-degree scanning angle, and requires 10 seconds to scan. Higher ratings increase range and power draw.<ref name="edcd-manifest">EDCD Coriolis Data, [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/EDCD/coriolis-data/9e5273b56426596061e2b02a6ba53e3e4103c9ab/modules/hardpoints/cargo_scanner.json Cargo Scanner records], commit of 6 June 2024.</ref>

EDSM's current outfitting records independently list the same ranges, scan times, mass, integrity, and power draw.<ref name="edsm-manifest">EDSM, [https://www.edsm.net/en/faq/outfitting/index/id/3/name/Utility+Mount/sub/Manifest+Scanners Manifest Scanners].</ref> The rating changes how far away the scan can begin; it does not change what the completed scan reveals.

== Engineering ==

Manifest Scanners accept six blueprint families and have no documented Experimental Effects:<ref name="inara-manifest">INARA, [https://inara.cz/elite/blueprints/#tab_blueprintsequipmentstandard Blueprints and upgrades], accessed 2026-09-16.</ref>

* '''Fast Scan''' reduces scan time at the cost of range and integrity.
* '''Lightweight''' reduces mass while reducing integrity.
* '''Long Range''' extends range while increasing power draw and narrowing the scanning angle.
* '''Reinforced''' increases integrity while adding mass.
* '''Shielded''' increases integrity while increasing power draw.
* '''Wide Angle''' enlarges the scanning arc while adding mass and increasing scan time.

Fast Scan is useful when a target may escape or become hostile before the stock ten-second cycle finishes. Long Range allows inspection to begin sooner, while Wide Angle makes it easier to keep a moving target inside the scan cone. The best choice depends on whether time, stand-off distance, aiming tolerance, or ship mass is the main constraint.

== Acquisition ==

Manifest Scanners are ordinary credit-purchased utility modules. Ratings E through A require no permit, Engineer, Technology Broker unlock, or Powerplay reward. The ratings available at a particular port depend on its current Outfitting stock.
